title: B2+ · L18 — Phrasal verbs (relationships)
description: Phrasal verbs sobre relaciones: fall out, patch things up, drift apart, hit it off, y otros esenciales.

questions.prompt: Un colega te cuenta: 'The two co-founders fell out over money — they haven't spoken in a year.'
questions.question: 'They fell out over money' means:
options: Had a serious argument / stopped being friends.
questions.explanation: 'Fall out (with someone) (over something)' = pelearse seriamente y romper relacion, no una discusion menor. Muy comun para amistades, familia, business partners, matrimonios. Implica RUPTURA sostenida, no discusion pasajera. Colocaciones: 'fell out over money/politics/inheritance'. Diferencia clave con 'have a fight' (pelea puntual) — falling out es mas grave y duradero. Registro: neutro-personal. Error hispano: interpretar literal como caerse fisicamente (falling out of a tree existe pero es contexto totalmente distinto).
examples: The two co-founders fell out over strategy and the company split in two. → business
They fell out years ago and haven't spoken since — nobody remembers why exactly. → estado prolongado

questions.prompt: Tras semanas de tension, dos amigos hacen las paces: 'They patched things up after the argument.'
questions.question: 'They patched things up after the argument' means:
questions.explanation: 'Patch things up' = reconciliarse, reparar la relacion tras conflicto. Metafora textil: poner un parche sobre una tela rota — arregla pero puede quedar visible. Opuesto exacto de 'fall out'. Colocaciones nativas: 'patch things up', 'patch up their differences', 'patch up the friendship'. Sugiere reparacion imperfecta pero funcional. Registro: neutro-personal. Diferencia con 'make up' (mas rapido y casual) o 'reconcile' (mas formal, elevado).
examples: They patched things up over a long dinner and a bottle of wine. → escenario clasico
It took months to patch things up after the falling-out — some scars remain. → reparacion parcial

questions.statement: 'To drift apart' describes a slow, gradual loss of closeness in a relationship.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Drift apart' = distanciarse gradualmente SIN conflicto, por circunstancias vitales, prioridades cambiantes, o simple distancia. Metafora oceanica potente: dos barcos flotando sin motor van en direcciones distintas por corrientes — no chocaron, solo se alejaron. Comun en amistades post-universidad, matrimonios largos, familia geografica. Diferencia crucial con 'fall out' (conflicto activo). 'Drift apart' es melancolico pero neutro moralmente. Registro: personal/emocional.
examples: After college, we just drifted apart — no drama, just different lives. → ausencia de conflicto
Long-distance made them drift apart over the years despite their best intentions.

questions.prompt: En un evento profesional conoces a alguien nuevo: 'We hit it off from day one.'
questions.question: 'We hit it off from day one' means:
questions.explanation: 'Hit it off' = conectar rapidamente y bien con alguien, caerse instantaneamente bien. Positivo y comun. Usado para nuevas amistades, primeras citas exitosas, entrevistas donde hay quimica, dinamicas de equipo. La expresion completa incluye 'with': 'we hit it off WITH each other'. Puede ser platonico o romantico segun contexto. Registro: casual-neutro. Colocacion nativa: 'we hit it off right away', 'we hit it off from the start', 'we really hit it off'.
examples: We hit it off at the conference and stayed in touch for years afterward. → networking exitoso
The two teams hit it off during onboarding — great cultural fit. → context corporativo

questions.text: It took years for us to open up to each other, but now we can talk about anything.
questions.explanation: Frase profunda de relacion emocional. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'open up to' con doble catenacion /ˈəʊpənʌptə/; 'each other' con weak /iːtʃˈʌðə/; 'talk about' con weak /tɔːkəˈbaʊt/. Colocacion clave: 'open up' = abrirse emocionalmente, compartir sentimientos vulnerables (metafora de abrir una caja). Central en therapy, deep friendship, parenting, coaching. Diferencia con 'open' solo (fisico) — 'open up' es especificamente emocional. Registro: personal/emocional.
examples: He struggles to open up about his feelings — a lot of cultural conditioning to unpack.
Therapy helped her open up in ways she never had before — transformative process.

questions.prompt: Cuentas de tu hermana pequena: 'She looks up to her older sister — has been her role model since she was five.'
questions.question: 'She looks up to her older sister' means:
questions.explanation: 'Look up to' = admirar, tener como modelo/referente. Metafora vertical: literalmente 'mirar hacia arriba' como los ninos miran a adultos. Usado para mentores, hermanos mayores, lideres, heroes. Opuesto exacto: 'look down on' = menospreciar, despreciar. Ambos son fundamentales del vocabulario emocional-social ingles. Colocaciones: 'look up to my grandfather', 'kids look up to their teachers'. Registro: neutro-personal. Error hispano: NO significa observar fisicamente.
examples: I've always looked up to my grandfather — he shaped who I am today.
Junior engineers look up to her for how she handles conflict with grace. → contexto profesional

questions.prompt: Empareja cada phrasal verb de relaciones con su traduccion:
questions.explanation: Seis phrasal verbs nucleares de vocabulario de relaciones. Distincion clave: 'fall out' vs 'drift apart' — el primero es conflicto activo, el segundo distanciamiento pasivo. 'Put up with' es esencial para expresar tolerancia bajo protesta ('I can't put up with this anymore' es literalmente frase clave de ruptura). 'Look up to' vs 'look down on' es par opuesto simetrico. 'Hit it off' vs 'fall out' representan inicio y final de relacion. Todos son fundamentales del habla nativa cotidiana.
examples: I couldn't put up with the disrespect anymore, so I finally spoke up. → linea roja
She's put up with a lot from her family over the years. → paciencia extendida

questions.target: We fell out over something small, but a year later we managed to patch things up and now we're closer than ever.
questions.explanation: Arco narrativo clasico de reconciliacion. Combina 'fall out' (ruptura) + 'patch things up' (reparacion) en una estructura de tres beats: conflicto -> tiempo -> resurreccion. 'Something small' — colocacion nativa comun para minimizar retrospectivamente. 'Now we're closer than ever' es cierre satisfactorio tipico de historia de reconciliacion. Ritmo natural: pausa breve tras 'small,', tono ascendente en 'closer than ever'. Contracciones: 'we're' obligatoria. Registro: personal/storytelling casual.
examples: We drifted apart after graduation, but we hit it off again at the reunion ten years later.
They fell out for a decade before finally patching things up at their mother's funeral. → contexto

questions.prompt: Un amigo te dice: 'They broke up after five years — she was heartbroken.'
questions.question: 'They broke up after five years' means:
questions.explanation: 'Break up (with someone)' = terminar relacion romantica. Colocacion ubicua. Opuestos: 'get back together' (reconciliarse), 'stay together' (seguir juntos). Puede ser transitivo ('she broke up with him') o intransitivo ('they broke up'). Registro: neutro-personal. Sustantivo: 'a breakup' (una ruptura). Diferencia con 'split up' (equivalente, ligeramente mas maduro/formal) y 'call it quits' (mas casual). Error hispano: no confundir con 'break down' (colapsar emocionalmente o averiarse un aparato).
examples: They broke up amicably last summer — no drama, no lawyers. → ruptura pacifica
After breaking up, they stayed close friends — rare but wholesome. → post-breakup

questions.statement: 'To take after someone' means to resemble them physically or in character.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Take after' = parecerse a alguien (usualmente familiar de generacion anterior). Puede ser fisico ('same eyes as her mother') o de personalidad/temperamento ('same stubborn streak as dad'). Colocacion tipica: 'she takes after her mother', 'he takes after his grandfather'. Estructura curiosa: verbo + preposicion sin objeto directo tras 'after'. Registro: personal/familiar. Diferencia con 'look like' (solo fisico) — 'take after' incluye caracter y comportamiento heredado.
examples: He takes after his father — same laugh, same temper, same terrible sense of humor.
She takes after her grandmother in her love of gardening and old jazz music. → caracter

questions.prompt: Ante una crisis personal, sabes en quien apoyarte: 'I can always count on my best friend.'
questions.question: 'I can always count on my best friend' means:
questions.explanation: 'Count on (someone/something)' = confiar en, depender de, contar con. Central en vocabulario de amistad, colaboracion, y compromiso. 'You can count on me' es LA frase clasica de lealtad y compromiso — casi ritual en anglo culture. Colocacion nativa: 'count on X to do Y', 'count on X for support'. Diferencia sutil con 'rely on' (mas formal, dependencia estructural) — 'count on' es mas emocional y personal. Registro: universal, todos contextos.
examples: In tough times, I know I can count on him to show up, no questions asked.
The team counts on her judgment in a crisis — steadiest hand we have. → contexto profesional

questions.text: We grew up together, went our separate ways for a while, but ended up living on the same street again.
questions.explanation: Frase narrativa vital con TRES phrasal verbs. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'grew up' con /uːʌ/ enlazado /ɡruːʌp/; 'went our' con /nta/ /wentaʊə/; 'ended up' con /dʌ/ /ˈendɪdʌp/. Vocabulario clave: 'grow up' = crecer / hacerse adulto (biografico); 'go one's separate ways' = separarse en caminos vitales; 'end up' = terminar / resultar finalmente. Los tres son fundamentales para storytelling autobiografico. Registro: personal/narrativo. El giro 'end up living on the same street again' anade coincidencia poetica.
examples: We grew up together and eventually ended up working at the same firm — small world.
After college we went our separate ways, but we still meet up every year without fail.

questions.prompt: Preguntas sobre los hermanos: 'The kids get along really well — always have.'
questions.question: 'The kids get along really well' means:
options: They have a good relationship / harmony.
questions.explanation: 'Get along (with someone)' = llevarse bien, tener buena relacion. Uso ubicuo para relaciones personales, familiares, profesionales. Colocaciones tipicas: 'how are you getting along with X?' (como te llevas con), 'we get along great', 'they don't get along'. Alternativa UK: 'get on with' (equivalente exacto). Registro: neutro-personal. Diferencia con 'along' solo (a lo largo de) — 'get along' es especificamente sobre relacion humana. Error hispano frecuente: 'get well with' (calco) — es 'get along with'.
examples: The kids get along beautifully — no drama, they actually enjoy each other's company.
How are you getting along with your new colleagues? → pregunta social estandar

questions.statement: 'To stand by someone' means to abandon them in difficult times.
questions.explanation: FALSO — es EXACTAMENTE lo contrario. 'Stand by someone' = apoyar lealmente, ser fiel especialmente en tiempos dificiles. Metafora fisica: quedarse al lado de alguien cuando otros se van. Frase de lealtad profunda. Cancion famosa 'Stand by Me' (Ben E. King) inmortaliza el concepto. Registro: personal-emocional profundo. Distinto de 'stand up for' (defender activamente contra un ataque) — stand by es presencia leal, stand up for es defensa activa. Ambos son actos de lealtad complementarios.
examples: She stood by her partner through the trial, even when it destroyed her career. → lealtad extrema
I'll stand by you no matter what — that's what family means. → declaracion de commitment

questions.target: I know I can count on you — you've stood by me through everything, and I don't take that for granted.
questions.explanation: Frase emocional profunda que combina TRES colocaciones nucleares de amistad/relacion: 'count on you' (confiar), 'stood by me' (apoyar lealmente), 'don't take for granted' (no dar por sentado — reconocer conscientemente el valor). Discurso maduro adulto — muestra dominio del vocabulario emocional adulto anglo. Ritmo natural: tono calido y calmado, pausas marcadas tras cada frase para dar peso emocional. Contracciones: 'you've', 'I don't' obligatorias. Registro: personal profundo — para amigo intimo, pareja, familiar cercano.
examples: You've stood by me when nobody else did. I never take that for granted. → variante emocional
I know I can always count on you, and that means everything to me. → cierre emotivo
